haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Unknown email and wrong password both get 401 with "Invalid email or password", via the same path with a dummy bcrypt hash.
haiku-low.q2: Login is refused with HTTP 429 and Retry-After for 15 minutes, with "Too many attempts. Try again later." The password is never checked, and refused attempts are not recorded.
haiku-low.q3: The session that the browser's presented cookie points to is deleted in the same transaction, even if it belongs to another user. A new session with a fresh random ID is then created.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random session ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url), with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from login, even with continuous use. Idle timeout is 30 minutes, and activity does not extend the 12-hour absolute limit.
haiku-low.q6: It returns 303 to /login and clears the cookie with Max-Age=0. It runs a separate DELETE for that hash first; if that delete fails, the error is only logged.
haiku-low.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes that session row by hash before replying 303 to /login with the cookie cleared. If the session is already gone, the delete affects zero rows and the same response is sent.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres tables (sessions, login_failures, login_lockouts) shared by both instances. Any instance finds a session by looking up the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, keyed by lowercase email with a failed_at timestamp. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at within the last 10 minutes, using the database clock now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares the cookie's hash to a row with last_seen_at within 30 minutes and created_at within 12 hours. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
haiku-low.q11: 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." The transaction rolls back, so no session is issued and no session cookie is set.
haiku-low.q12: A sweep timer in each app process, every 5 minutes, deletes expired sessions, old login_failures and passed lockouts. Rejected sessions are also deleted lazily when they are seen.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get the same 401 with the login page and "Invalid email or password". An unknown email runs bcrypt against a dummy hash, so timing is the same too.
sonnet.q2: It is refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header (whole seconds left, rounded up). The page says "Too many attempts. Try again later." The password is never checked, so even a correct password is refused. The attempt is not recorded as a failure. This lasts 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: In the same transaction the server deletes the session that the old cookie points to, even if it belongs to another user. It then inserts a brand-new session with a fresh random ID. The old ID is never reused.
sonnet.q4: Only a random session ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url). It carries no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login (the absolute limit). Activity keeps the 30-minute idle clock restarting but never extends the 12 hours.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row. The server runs a separate DELETE of that session hash, and a failure of that DELETE is only logged. It then clears the cookie (Max-Age=0) and redirects 303 to /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id_hash before replying, whether or not the session has expired. If there is no cookie, it skips the delete. If the session is already gone, the delete removes nothing and is harmless. The reply is 303 to /login with the cookie cleared, the same response as for a request with no session.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, which both instances share. Either instance hashes the cookie's session ID with SHA-256 and looks it up with one SQL UPDATE statement that also checks expiry. No sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, keyed by the lowercased email, with a failed_at timestamp. On each failure the server counts that email's rows from the last 10 minutes using the database clock (now()). This is a sliding window.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now() - 30 minutes (idle limit) and created_at against now() - 12 hours (absolute limit), using the database clock. If both pass, it sets last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." The transaction rolls back and no session or cookie is issued.
sonnet.q12: Two things. A lazy DELETE happens if that session ID is presented again and rejected. A sweep timer in each app process runs every 5 minutes and deletes sessions past the 30-minute idle limit or the 12-hour absolute limit.
